title: Rigveda 1.19: To Agni and the Maruts
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.19: To Agni and the Maruts: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.19 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to Agni and the Maruts. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 10r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.19.1-9 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 1, varga 36); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 10r
translation.original_text:
1prati̱ tyaṁ cāru̍m adhva̱raṁ go̍pī̱thāya̱ pra hū̍yase | ma̱rudbhi̍r agna̱ ā ga̍hi ||
2na̱hi de̱vo na martyo̍ ma̱has tava̱ kratu̍m pa̱raḥ | ma̱rudbhi̍r agna̱ ā ga̍hi ||
3ye ma̱ho raja̍so vi̱dur viśve̍ de̱vāso̍ a̱druha̍ḥ | ma̱rudbhi̍r agna̱ ā ga̍hi ||
4ya u̱grā a̱rkam ā̍nṛ̱cur anā̍dhṛṣṭāsa̱ oja̍sā | ma̱rudbhi̍r agna̱ ā ga̍hi ||
5ye śu̱bhrā gho̱rava̍rpasaḥ sukṣa̱trāso̍ ri̱śāda̍saḥ | ma̱rudbhi̍r agna̱ ā ga̍hi ||
6ye nāka̱syādhi̍ roca̱ne di̱vi de̱vāsa̱ āsa̍te | ma̱rudbhi̍r agna̱ ā ga̍hi ||
7ya ī̱ṅkhaya̍nti̱ parva̍tān ti̱raḥ sa̍mu̱dram a̍rṇa̱vam | ma̱rudbhi̍r agna̱ ā ga̍hi ||
8ā ye ta̱nvanti̍ ra̱śmibhi̍s ti̱raḥ sa̍mu̱dram oja̍sā | ma̱rudbhi̍r agna̱ ā ga̍hi ||
9a̱bhi tvā̍ pū̱rvapī̍taye sṛ̱jāmi̍ so̱myam madhu̍ | ma̱rudbhi̍r agna̱ ā ga̍hi ||
translation.text:
1To this fair sacrifice to drink the milky draught thou art invoked: O Agni, with the Maruts come.
2No mortal man, no God exceeds thy mental power, O Mighty one – O Agni, with the Maruts come
3All Gods devoid of guile, who know the mighty region of mid-air: O Agni, with those Maruts come.
4The terrible, who sing their song, not to be overcome by might: O Agni, with those Maruts come.
5Brilliant, and awful in their form, mighty, devourers of their foes': O Agni, with those Maruts come.
6Who sit as Deities in heaven, above the sky-vault's luminous sphere: O Agni, with those Maruts come.
7Who scatter clouds about the sky, away over the billowy sea: O Agni, with those Maruts come.
8Who with their bright beams spread them forth over the ocean in their might O Agni, with those Maruts come.
9For thee, to be thine early draught, I pour the Soma-mingled meath: O Agni, with the Maruts come.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 10r (OPenn image 11, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.18.6 ‹sadasaḥ patim adbhutam priyam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 10v, begins in RV 1.20.1 ‹-akāri ratna-dhātamaḥ›. Verses 1.19.1-9 end on this page.
